meta.project: devops-request-grant skill — AWS IAM grant request log
meta.purpose: Structured, append-only record of every AWS IAM permission grant requested and executed via the devops-request-grant skill. Replaces devops/manual.md's prose log with a tracked list in the same shape as the repo's other feature-list.json files, paired with this skill's own init.sh/evaluator/cleanup harness. Lives inside the skill directory, not in devops/, per the skill's design.
howToUse: Every time a grant is needed (SKILL.md step 2), append a new feature entry here BEFORE dispatching the grant-subagent, status 'requested'.
The grant-subagent flips it to 'applied' once create-policy-version --set-as-default succeeds, filling in appliedEvidence.

The calling session flips it to 'verified' ONLY after re-attempting the actual originally-blocked operation for real with AWS_PROFILE=devops-agent and confirming it now works — never on the subagent's report alone.
If the attempt fails or is declined, flip to 'denied' with the reason in rubric. Never delete a failed entry — it's part of the audit trail devops/manual.md used to be.

statusLegend.requested: Minimal statement drafted, not yet dispatched to a grant-subagent.
statusLegend.applied: create-policy-version --set-as-default succeeded per the subagent's report, not yet independently re-verified.
statusLegend.verified: The originally-blocked operation was re-attempted for real, by devops-agent, and now succeeds.
statusLegend.denied: Assume-role or apply failed, or the human declined — see rubric for why.

meta.invariantsRef: devops/AGENTS.md 'Requesting an AWS permission grant' section is the authoritative procedure this file supports. This skill's own non-negotiables: never root, never a self-grant, statements are minimal (no service:* wildcards, no Resource: "*" unless the action is inherently resource-less), every 'verified' status requires re-attempting the real blocked operation.

features.title: ssm:SendCommand on the AWS-owned AWS-RunShellScript document
features.description: devops.terraform_networking_rds's 4th acceptance criterion (pgvector enabled, proven reachable from inside the VPC) needs devops-agent to call ssm:SendCommand against the AWS-owned AWS-RunShellScript document. The existing SsmDeploy statement's ssm:resourceTag/deploy condition can never satisfy this — AWS-owned documents can't carry a caller-set tag, so the document half of the SendCommand authorization check always fails regardless of how the target instance is tagged.
acceptance: Statement is scoped to exactly ssm:SendCommand on arn:aws:ssm:us-east-1::document/AWS-RunShellScript, unconditioned (mirrors infra/terraform/main.tf's own working SsmSendCommandDocument statement for the GitHub Actions deploy role).
Applied to scribe-devops-infra, set as the default version.
devops-agent can then successfully call ssm:SendCommand against that document for a deploy-tagged target instance.
verify: aws iam get-policy-version --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::404063516240:policy/scribe-devops-infra --version-id <new-version> | grep SsmSendCommandDocument -- run with the iam-grantor-devops-agent ASSUMED-ROLE credentials still active from the apply step, in the same subagent session; neither nimat-admin (only sts:AssumeRole) nor devops-agent (structurally can't read its own policies) can call iam:GetPolicyVersion on their own
Re-run the throwaway SSM-probe mechanism (devops/progress.md's 2026-08-19 entries) with AWS_PROFILE=devops-agent and confirm ssm:SendCommand no longer returns AccessDeniedException
features.rubric: Requested and re-attempted twice as of 2026-08-19 (once in the original PR #21 session, once in a dedicated re-verify subagent after this skill's grantor-role architecture was set up) — both times the identical AccessDeniedException came back verbatim, meaning the statement above has genuinely not landed on scribe-devops-infra yet (or landed without --set-as-default).
